item.title: Iran's Houthi allies deny losing ground as Mideast crisis engulfs Yemen
item.description: Iran's Houthi allies deny that they've lost ground to Yemen's Saudi-backed military, as oil prices ease despite the Middle East crisis erupting in a battle over control of another key waterway.

item.title: In Maine Senate debate, Collins and Jackson both criticize Trump — but spar over how
item.description: In an often-testy debate, GOP Sen. Susan Collins of Maine touted her five terms in Congress and took aim at some Trump policies — while Democrat Troy Jackson argued Collins has failed to effectively push back.

item.title: GOP Super PAC pours $5 million into South Carolina Senate race, sources say
item.description: The influx of cash comes as President Trump escalated the attacks against Darline Graham's Democratic opponent, Annie Andrews.

item.title: Storm brewing off Mexico could impact Gulf Coast as hurricane this weekend
item.description: Tropical Depression Nine formed in the Gulf, and it's expected to become a hurricane later this week.

item.title: Hundreds of Israeli flags vandalized outside church in McKinney, Texas, ahead of Oct. 7 observance
item.description: Heritage Church in McKinney, Texas, says hundreds of Israeli flags honoring victims of the Oct. 7 attack were pulled from the ground overnight Tuesday.

item.title: From the archives: Eva Marie Saint on why she never "went Hollywood"
item.description: Actress Eva Marie Saint, who won an Oscar for her debut opposite Marlon Brando in "On the Waterfront," and starred in such classics as "North by Northwest" and "Exodus," died on Oct. 6, 2026 at age 102. In this "Sunday Morning" profile that aired March 2, 2014, Saint talked with correspondent Mo Rocca about working with Alfred Hitchcock, Cary Grant and Paul Newman; balancing a film career with family; and how she maintained being a "normal" person in Hollywood.

item.title: Medical experts on plague risks after reported death of lab worker in Russia
item.description: A scientist in Siberia died after possible exposure to the plague bacteria during a lab accident, according to Russian media. Russian officials downplayed the reports, saying she died of a "pneumonia of unknown origin." Health experts spoke with CBS News to discuss the risks posed to the public and what people should know about the reports.

item.title: Watch: Reporter rides along with ICE as arrest carried out
item.description: CBS News immigration correspondent Camilo Montoya-Galvez rides along with ICE agents as they track a man slated for arrest in Georgia.

item.title: Details emerge in case of former Cornell student alleging rape by frat members
item.description: A woman, identified only as Jane Doe, alleges she was gang-raped by seven fraternity members in 2024 and accuses Cornell University of failing to protect her.

item.title: Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan to be executed Dec. 3, email states
item.description: Nidal Hasan is set to die by firing squad in what will be the first military execution since 1961.

item.title: What to make of security incident at U.S.-run base in England
item.description: British police have arrested a 22-year-old man suspected of planning terrorist acts following a security incident at a U.S.-run military base in England. CBS News national security analyst Aaron MacLean shares his takeaways on the incident.

item.title: California couple at center of surrogacy scandal arrested
item.description: Guojun Xuan and Silvia Zhang, who had at least 25 children via surrogates, were arrested at their home in Arcadia, California.

item.title: Key races to watch with 4 weeks until midterms as Democrats look to flip Senate
item.description: Democrats are gaining ground in multiple key races as they look to take control of Congress with only 4 weeks to go before the midterms. Caitlin Huey-Burns, Anthony Salvanto and Jessica Taylor, Senate and governors editor for The Cook Political Report, join "The Daily Report" to discuss the top races to watch.

item.title: Why you just got a $90 Social Security check — and who missed out
item.description: Millions of seniors are getting $90 direct deposits from Social Security this week, prompting questions about the source of the money.

item.title: Paramount closes $110 billion deal to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery
item.description: The merger unites two major movie studios, news operations CBS News and CNN and cable networks including Comedy Central and TNT.

item.title: Millions of seniors receiving $90 deposits from Social Security Administration
item.description: Roughly 20 million Medicare enrollees are receiving $90 checks this week from the Social Security Administration as part of an effort from President Trump to lower healthcare costs. CBS News' Megan Cerullo reports.

item.title: White House defends Trump's comment to let Iran "take out" Los Angeles and San Diego
item.description: The White House is defending President Trump after he suggested letting Iran "take out" Los Angeles and San Diego. CBS News' Nikole Killion has more.

item.title: Former Cornell students dragged into alleged rape scandal, ask school to clear their names
item.description: A group of former Cornell students say they've been falsely connected to the alleged 2024 fraternity house rape. CBS News' Lilia Luciano has the details.

item.title: The life and travels of an alleged Chinese agent in the U.S.
item.description: A CBS News investigation reveals new details about the life and background of a California mom accused of conducting surveillance for China.

item.title: Yellow labs make first leaf pile jump of this fall season
item.description: Jody Hartman rakes his leaves into a big pile, and then gives his dogs Stella and Mabel the go-ahead to jump in. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: Christa Pike is conscious, speaking after botched execution, attorneys say
item.description: Christa Pike, a death row inmate who was subject​ to a failed execution attempt in Tennessee last week, is conscious and speaking from her hospital bed, her attorneys said Tuesday.

item.title: Tennessee woman conscious, speaking after execution attempt, lawyers say
item.description: Christa Pike, the convicted killer who survived two lethal injections last week in Tennessee, is now conscious and speaking, according to her lawyers. Tom Hanson reports.

item.title: 10/6: CBS Evening News
item.description: A California couple was arrested on child abuse charges in a surrogacy scandal; Christa Pike is awake and speaking after her failed execution.

item.title: Marco Rubio calls for Russian transparency over plague lab worker's death
item.description: Dozens of people in Russia are in quarantine after the death of a woman who worked at a lab that studies plague and other infectious diseases. Russian officials say she died of pneumonia, but U.S. officials are not so sure. Dr. Ashish Jha, a senior fellow at the Harvard Belfer Center, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Eva Marie Saint, "North by Northwest" star, dies at 102
item.description: Eva Marie Saint won an Oscar for her film debut opposite Marlon Brando in "On the Waterfront." She bucked many Hollywood conventions throughout her lengthy career.

item.title: 10/6: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Fallout after Trump suggests letting Iran "take out" Los Angeles and San Diego; Kansas could send first Democrat to Senate since 1932.

item.title: Former Cornell frat members ask university to clear their names
item.description: Some former Cornell University students say they are being falsely connected to a 2024 sexual assault​​ and targeted online.

item.title: Olympian accused of damaging Reflecting Pool seeks probe of potential misconduct
item.description: David Hearn is asking the Justice and Interior Dept. inspectors general to investigate his arrest and the dismissal of the case against him.

item.title: ABC asks judge to block FCC early license review
item.description: An ABC lawyer argued the FCC was effectively forcing the broadcast company to sit with its "head on a guillotine" while it awaits a decision about its license renewals.

item.title: Ex-CIA official found with $40 million in gold bars admits to sprawling scheme
item.description: A former CIA official admitted to inventing fake classified programs to divert nearly $200 million in government money that was used to buy Florida mansions and gold bars.
